main_text.p: dem consiliumque publicum expurgarent. Et his clariora etiam sunt, quæ habet Diodorus bellum, quod Demetrius Rhodiis intulit, exponens. Nam & συμμαχικῶν[?] ἐκκλησίαν[?] Rhodiorum memorat, & populum de rebus summis sententiam ferentem, & consilii mali autores graviter reprehendentem, ac legatos de pace agentes audientem, judiciumque suum interponentem inducit: ut taceam, quod inter democratias rempubl. Rhodiorum sat expressis verbis referat. Quid igitur, quæret aliquis, hEIc statuendum? Id scilicet, quod ante dixi, πολιτείαν[?] illam Aristotelicam, aut proximam ei apud Rhodios per ea tempora valuisse; popularem nimirum potestatem summarum autoritate & consilio temperatam locum ibi habuisse. Confirmant hoc reipubl. hujus præclara elogia, apud optimos autores passim occurrentia. Cujusmodi est illud Strabonis supra recitatum: Ἰουμαίων[?] ἡ μὲν δυναστεία[?], inquit, ᾗ δύο ... πρὸς τε τὴν ἄλλην πολιτείαν[?], ἐς τὰ ναυτικά[?]. Et hoc, quod apud Diodorum est ad initium belli Demetriani: ἡ πόλις ἡ τῶν Ῥοδίων ἰσχύσασα ναυτικῆς δυνάμεως[?], ᾗ πο-

page.notes: Several Greek words are doubtful because the print is small and partly broken: συμμαχικῶν, ἐκκλησίαν, the Strabo quotation and its opening word, and the phrase after "ᾗ δύο". They are marked [?] and should be checked against the scan. The Latin reads clearly apart from "hEIc", which may be "heic" with a mis-set capital; the printed form is left as the scan suggests. The number "193" and the running head are read from the top of the page. The mark "n" at the foot is taken as the gathering signature, which is uncertain. The left edge carries mirrored show-through from the facing page, which is not transcribed. A cut-off line of Greek at the foot is counted as the catchword.
